subject: BUG-255: ModuleProgress.complete() is a client-side XP mint with no content or house validation
description:
PROVEN by Mallory 2026-09-03 during the BUG-253 vote. PRE-EXISTING and NOT fixed by any BUG-253 option; filed separately so it is not silently closed as 'covered'. ModuleProgress.complete(houseId, moduleId, opts) validates only that both args are non-empty strings (ModuleProgress.js:559) -- no house allow-list and no check that moduleId names real content. bridgeStructuredProgress (ModuleProgress.js:377-436) then awards real XP (100/500/1000 by opts.type) gated ONLY on isFirstCompletion, which reads the global house-agnostic completedModules array. So a student in devtools can run ModuleProgress.complete('anything','fake-module-1',{type:'lab'}) and mint 500 XP for content that does not exist, under a house that does not exist. SERVER SIDE TOO: pushToUserProfile -> FirestoreManager -> CF recordProgress (functions/index.js:1225-1287) takes house straight from request.data and interpolates it into a Firestore field path, updates['houseProgress.'+house+'.completed'] = increment(1), with no allow-list. Mallory ranks this LOW SEVERITY because writes stay inside the caller's own users/{uid}.houseProgress subtree and cannot reach another user's doc or escape to other top-level fields. This is the XP/progress analogue of the never-client-grade rule: the client is asserting an outcome the server accepts without deriving it. Any fix must decide what the server can actually verify -- a house allow-list is trivial, but 'did this student really complete this module' is the harder half. NOTE for whoever fixes it: XP is the currency for levels, achievements and the trophy cabinet, so inflation is not cosmetic.
[2026-09-06 03:12] PANEL RESULT: C wins 3-1 (Chris, Nancy, primary for C; Mallory D). Mallory's D SUPERSEDES C rather than opposing it: she proved xp/level are directly client-writable in firestore.rules, so server-derived completion is necessary but insufficient. Filed as BUG-262. Sequence: fix the rules FIRST (small, has precedent in the same file where ctfBoxesPwned/ctfFlagsCaptured were removed 2026-08-05), then phase C by content type. Chris's observable stands: the console repro must fail while a real lab still awards. Scale for phasing: 2952 complete() call sites but only 14 pass type:'lab', and the server already holds evidence for quizzes (quiz_keys/gradeQuiz) and flags (246 seeded flag_registry boxes). Unsolved fork Mallory named: a 'viewed a presentation' completion has NO server truth to derive from at all.
